claims.claim: WCAG is published by the W3C Web Accessibility Initiative and is organized under four principles: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, and Robust (POUR), with three conformance levels A, AA, and AAA.

WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 1.4.3 (AA) requires a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for normal text and at least 3:1 for large text, where large text means 18 point or 14 point bold (approximately 24px or 18.5px).

WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 1.4.11 (AA) requires a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 for user interface components and for graphical objects needed to understand content, measured against adjacent colors.

WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 1.4.1 Use of Color (Level A) requires that color not be the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response, or distinguishing a visual element.

Per W3C WAI guidance, informative and functional images need descriptive alt text conveying their meaning or function, while purely decorative or redundant images should use an empty alt attribute (alt="").

WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 1.4.12 Text Spacing (AA) supports readability by ensuring no loss of content when line height is set to at least 1.5x font size, spacing after paragraphs to at least 2x, letter spacing to at least 0.12x, and word spacing to at least 0.16x the font size.
The 2024 U.S. Department of Justice ADA Title II rule adopts WCAG 2.1 Level AA as the technical standard for state and local government web content and mobile apps.
Low-contrast text harms readability for many users, not only those with diagnosed impairments, so sufficient contrast is a general usability concern.
Universal (inclusive) design is the design of products and environments to be usable by all people, to the greatest extent possible, without adaptation or specialized design.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Pixel equivalents for 'large text' are stated approximately.
positions: WCAG understanding text uses 1pt = 1.333px, giving ~18.5px for 14pt and ~24px for 18pt
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The normative definition is in points (18pt, or 14pt bold); pixel figures are approximate conversions. The lesson states the point definition first and gives the pixel values as approximate.

unsupportedExistingClaims: The generated draft contained only generic boilerplate ('a foundational concept... this lesson introduces its meaning') with no accessibility content, contrast ratios, or standards. All of it was discarded.
correctionsNeeded: Replaced boilerplate with the actual WCAG standard, exact ratios, and attribution to the W3C WAI.
Added the specific 4.5:1 / 3:1 thresholds and the definition of large text.
Distinguished this topic (the accessibility standard and ratios) from the separate contrast, color-theory, and typography-basics topics.
rightsIssues: All sources are authoritative standards/government pages used as REFERENCE_ONLY; facts synthesized and prose written originally. No copyrighted images, logos, or proprietary color values reproduced.
